items.q: Why does Karpathy feel more behind as a programmer than ever?
items.a: Not despite AI — because **December 2025** marked a step change where **agentic workflows stopped needing constant correction**, and he entered a rabbit hole of side projects. Many ChatGPT-era mental models are now stale.

LLMs as programmable computers where **prompting + the context window** replace traditional code. Example: MenuGen (a full Vercel app) made obsolete by a **single Gemini image prompt** — "that app shouldn't exist."

items.q: How do vibe coding and agentic engineering differ?
items.a: **Vibe coding raises the floor** — anyone can build. **Agentic engineering** preserves the professional quality bar while going far beyond **10× faster**.

Models automate what you can **verify** (like code automates what you can **specify**). RL peaks in verifiable domains (code, math) and fails on commonsense edge cases — jaggedness = **verifiable + labs care**.

items.q: What can't you outsource to agents?
items.a: "You can outsource your thinking, but you can't outsource your **understanding**." Humans keep **taste, spec design, judgment, oversight**, and fundamental comprehension — not API trivia.

items.q: What are LLM wikis actually for?
items.a: Knowledge bases are tools for **enhancing understanding**, not replacing it — Karpathy's own wiki/knowledge-base project.

items.q: What becomes the new programming paradigm?
items.a: "What is the piece of text to **copy-paste to your agent**?" Agent-native docs, sensors/actuators over the world, and agents negotiating on our behalf replace human-oriented instructions.

items.q: How should you hire agentic engineers?
items.a: Use **big real projects + red-team agents**, not LeetCode puzzles — evaluate coordinating fallible agents without sacrificing quality.
